messages:
anna_finance: heads-up — noticed a sudden spike in billable embed units for customer skylark starting ~2026-02-12 03:00 UTC after yesterday's rate-limiter cutover. looks like a ~4x jump vs baseline. can we confirm if this is a metering or tagging issue? :eyes:
ben_platform: which cutover change? the small pilot to switch to the new global rate-limiter (rl-v2)?
cory_eng: that was the change. we enabled rl-v2 + a retry-tagging tweak to suppress meter increments on downstream 429 retries. if that suppressed incorrectly, it could cause overcounting. i'll pull logs.
anna_finance: attaching quick diff from billing exports (redacted):
```
2026-02-11 02:50 skylark embed_units: 12,438
2026-02-12 03:10 skylark embed_units: 49,200  <-- spike
```

ben_platform: can you paste the rl-v2 config flag we flipped? maybe the metric name changed and the billing pipeline missed the suppression tag.
cory_eng: rl flag in prod: `rate_limiter.version = v2` and `retry_metering.policy = legacy-tag` (intended to be `legacy-suppress`). looks like a typo in the deploy manifest. mounting a trace now.
sasha_ops: @cory_eng FYI the deploy logs show a warning around the metering plugin yesterday at 02:58 UTC: `plugin: metering: unknown policy 'legacy-tag' -> defaulting to billable`
metering-bot: SYSTEM: metering-agent/host-07 reported 403 malformed-policy for metering policy at 2026-02-12T02:58:17Z (trace_id=6f3a..).
cory_eng: ok that explains it — rl-v2 defaulted to counting because the intended suppression policy name was misspelled. will open a rollback/patch. estimated delta for skylark from 03:00-06:00 = ~36,500 extra embed units.
anna_finance: thanks. do we have ability to run a backfill that zeroes out those erroneous units or do we issue a credit? what's the right ops path here?
ben_platform: two options: 1) backfill the billing ledger by subtracting the erroneous counts (requires ledger replay for that window), or 2) issue a one-time manual credit on the invoice. finance preference?
sasha_ops: operationally safe option is credit — backfill touches a lot of downstream joins (ingest offsets, caches). but we could do a targeted ledger adjustment if finance wants an automated fix.
cory_eng: if we choose backfill i can produce a validated delta file (CSV) with request_ids and counts for the window. it will include an audit column and the metering-bot trace ids. sample row: `req_abc123, skylark, 1, embed, 2026-02-12T03:02:12Z, meter_tag=default`
metering-bot: NOTE: candidate delta file size estimate = 34k lines, compressed 1.2MB.
anna_finance: I'd like a suggested approach and ETA. if we credit, we should still fix the root cause and run a replay check to ensure no other customers affected.
ben_platform: suggested approach: (A) emergency patch to correct policy name (done in next 10m), (B) generate delta CSV from 02:58–06:00 and run a checksum against billing exports, (C) finance decides credit vs ledger backfill. ETA for (A)+(B) ~2 hours.
cory_eng: started patch rollout to metering plugin canary. will post canary logs. :hammer_and_wrench:
anna_finance: please @mention me when you have the CSV. finance will likely prefer ledger adjustment for auditability if it's low-risk. need approval from head of billing for any ledger rewrite.
sasha_ops: noted. i'll hold the rollback plan in case the patch causes regressions.
ben_platform: cory, if you can include a short script we can run to validate other customers in that region (filter by `meter_tag=default` + unusual spike pattern) that would be helpful.
cory_eng: will do — quick grep pipeline: `zcat metering-logs-2026-02-12.gz | jq -r \"select(.policy==\"default\") | .customer_id\" | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head`
anna_finance: thanks team. recording this as a provisional credit request until we have the CSV and audit. will escalate for ledger approval if needed. :white_check_mark:
